set: NCLEX-RN Practice – Clinical Judgment and Safe Nursing Care

questions.stem: The charge nurse on a medical-surgical unit is assigning care to a licensed practical/vocational nurse (LPN/VN). Which of the following clients would be most appropriate to assign to the LPN/VN?
options: A client admitted 30 minutes ago with chest pain who requires an initial assessment
A client with stable heart failure who requires scheduled oral medications and routine monitoring
A client who developed sudden confusion and unilateral weakness 15 minutes ago
A client receiving a first blood transfusion who requires assessment during initiation
questions.explanation: An LPN/VN can generally provide routine care, administer permitted medications, and monitor clients with stable, predictable conditions under appropriate supervision. Initial comprehensive assessments, evaluation of acute neurological changes, and responsibilities requiring RN-level assessment and clinical judgment should remain with the RN. Delegation must also comply with the applicable nurse practice act and institutional policy.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Management of Care – Assignment, Delegation and Supervision

questions.stem: A client scheduled for a laparoscopic cholecystectomy tells the nurse, "I signed the consent form, but I still do not understand why the surgery is necessary." Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Explain the surgical procedure and obtain a second signed consent form
Document that the client signed the consent form and continue preparation
Ask a family member to explain the reason for surgery to the client
Notify the surgeon that the client needs additional information before surgery
questions.explanation: The provider performing the procedure is responsible for explaining its purpose, risks, benefits, and alternatives so the client can make an informed decision. The nurse should advocate for the client by notifying the surgeon when the client expresses inadequate understanding. A signature alone does not establish informed consent.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Management of Care – Informed Consent

questions.stem: The nurse receives reports on four clients at the beginning of the shift. Which client should the nurse assess first?
options: A client 2 hours after thyroidectomy who has new inspiratory stridor
A client with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease whose oxygen saturation is 91% at the prescribed oxygen flow
A client with a urinary tract infection who reports burning during urination
A client 1 day after knee replacement who reports incisional pain rated 6 out of 10
questions.explanation: New inspiratory stridor after thyroidectomy suggests potentially life-threatening upper airway obstruction from swelling or a hematoma. Immediate airway assessment and emergency intervention take priority. The other clients require care but do not present the same immediate threat to airway patency.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Management of Care – Establishing Priorities

questions.stem: An alert, competent adult client with end-stage kidney disease tells the nurse that the client wishes to discontinue dialysis despite understanding that death is likely to occur sooner. The client's family insists that treatment continue. Which of the following actions should the nurse take?
options: Continue dialysis until the family members reach a unanimous decision
Request a psychiatric evaluation before discussing treatment withdrawal
Support the client's decision and notify the health care team of the client's wishes
Ask the ethics committee to authorize discontinuation before informing the provider
questions.explanation: A decisionally capable adult has the right to refuse or withdraw treatment, even when that decision may shorten life. The nurse should respect the client's autonomy, ensure the decision is communicated to the health care team, and facilitate appropriate discussions about goals of care and symptom management. Family disagreement does not override the capable client's treatment decision.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Management of Care – Client Rights and Advance Directives/Self-Determination/Life Planning

questions.stem: A client is admitted with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis and has a persistent cough, night sweats, and an abnormal chest radiograph. Which infection prevention measures should the nurse implement? Select all that apply.
options: Place the client in an airborne infection isolation room with negative pressure
Wear a fit-tested N95 respirator or higher-level respiratory protection when entering the room
Place a surgical mask on the client when transport outside the room is necessary
Use a positive-pressure protective environment room for routine isolation
Keep the room door closed except when entering or leaving
Require routine use of sterile gloves for all interactions with the client
questions.explanation: Suspected pulmonary tuberculosis requires airborne precautions, including an appropriate negative-pressure isolation room and respiratory protection for staff. The client should wear a surgical mask during necessary transport, and the isolation room door should remain closed. Positive-pressure rooms protect selected immunocompromised clients, while sterile gloves are not routinely necessary for tuberculosis precautions.
questions.topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control – Transmission-Based Precautions; CDC Guideline for Isolation Precautions

questions.stem: The nurse discovers that a hospitalized client received 10 units of rapid-acting insulin instead of the prescribed 6 units. The client is awake and has no symptoms. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Complete an institutional medication incident report
Inform the prescribing provider of the administration error
Document the error and its circumstances in the medical record
Check the client's blood glucose level immediately
questions.explanation: Following an insulin administration error, the nurse's immediate priority is assessing the client for potential harm, including hypoglycemia. Blood glucose measurement guides urgent treatment and monitoring. Provider notification, documentation, and incident reporting are also necessary but follow the immediate safety assessment.
questions.topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control – Accident/Error/Injury Prevention

questions.stem: A nurse is teaching a pregnant client at 28 weeks of gestation about warning signs that require immediate evaluation. Which client statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I should seek immediate evaluation if I develop a severe headache with blurred vision
I should expect persistent swelling of my face and hands during the third trimester
I should reduce my water intake if I begin experiencing intermittent leg cramps
I should wait until my next appointment if I notice a sudden decrease in fetal movements
questions.explanation: A severe headache with visual disturbances after 20 weeks of gestation can indicate preeclampsia with severe features and requires prompt evaluation. Sudden facial or hand swelling and decreased fetal movements also warrant assessment rather than routine reassurance. Recognizing these warning signs supports early identification of potentially serious maternal or fetal complications.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Health Promotion and Maintenance – Ante-/Intra-/Postpartum Care; ACOG Guidance on Preeclampsia

questions.stem: During a routine health visit, the nurse assesses a healthy 9-month-old infant born at term. Which developmental finding should the nurse expect?
options: Walking independently across the examination room
Sitting without support and transferring objects between hands
Using three-word sentences to request familiar objects
Drawing a circle after watching an adult demonstrate
questions.explanation: By approximately 9 months, most infants can sit without support and move objects between their hands. Independent walking, multiword sentences, and copying geometric shapes are developmental achievements expected at later ages. Assessment of milestones helps identify children who may need further developmental evaluation.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Health Promotion and Maintenance – Developmental Stages and Transitions; CDC Developmental Milestones

questions.stem: A client hospitalized after a suicide attempt tells the nurse, "I have been thinking about ending my life again, and I know how I would do it." Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
options: Encourage the client to write about the thoughts in a journal
Ask the client to identify positive events from the past week
Remain with the client and initiate the facility's immediate suicide safety precautions
Suggest that the client discuss these feelings during the next therapy session
questions.explanation: Current suicidal thoughts accompanied by a method or plan indicate significant immediate safety risk. The nurse should remain with the client, ensure close observation, reduce access to dangerous objects, and arrange urgent assessment according to facility protocol. Supportive discussions are appropriate after immediate safety is established.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Psychosocial Integrity – Crisis Intervention and Mental Health Concepts

questions.stem: A client whose spouse died 2 days ago tells the nurse, "I cannot imagine living in our house without my spouse." Which response by the nurse is most therapeutic?
options: You will probably feel much better once you return to your usual activities.
You should consider moving to a smaller home after the funeral.
Your spouse would likely want you to focus on the positive memories.
Tell me what you think will be most difficult about returning home.
questions.explanation: An open-ended invitation encourages the grieving client to express feelings and identify specific concerns. Therapeutic communication focuses on listening, acknowledging the loss, and exploring the client's experience without imposing solutions. Premature reassurance or advice can interfere with emotional expression.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Psychosocial Integrity – Therapeutic Communication and Grief and Loss

questions.stem: A nurse is planning care for an older adult with limited mobility who is at high risk for pressure injuries. Which interventions should the nurse include in the care plan? Select all that apply.
options: Reposition the client at intervals individualized to the client's condition and support surface
Massage reddened areas over bony prominences to stimulate circulation
Keep the head of the bed elevated to 45 degrees continuously
Use a pressure-redistributing support surface appropriate to the client's risk
Keep the skin clean and dry while managing moisture associated with incontinence
Assess nutritional status and address inadequate protein and calorie intake
questions.explanation: Pressure injury prevention includes individualized repositioning, suitable support surfaces, moisture management, and adequate nutrition. Massaging reddened bony areas may damage vulnerable tissue. Prolonged unnecessary head-of-bed elevation increases shear and should be avoided when not clinically indicated.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Basic Care and Comfort – Mobility/Immobility; International Guideline for Prevention and Treatment of Pressure Ulcers/Injuries

questions.stem: The nurse is teaching a client who recently began using a cane because of weakness in the left leg. Which instruction should the nurse provide?
options: Hold the cane in the left hand and move it after advancing the right leg
Hold the cane in the right hand and advance it with the left leg
Hold the cane in the left hand and advance it with the left leg
Hold the cane in the right hand and advance it with the right leg
questions.explanation: A cane is generally held on the side opposite the weaker or affected leg. Moving the cane forward with the weaker leg increases the base of support and reduces weight-bearing demands on that leg. The stronger leg then advances to complete the walking sequence.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Basic Care and Comfort – Assistive Devices

questions.stem: A client with atrial fibrillation takes warfarin daily. The nurse reviews the client's laboratory results and finds an INR of 5.8. The client has no evidence of active bleeding. Which action should the nurse take?
options: Withhold the scheduled warfarin dose and notify the prescribing provider
Administer the scheduled warfarin dose with additional oral fluids
Prepare to administer intravenous protamine sulfate immediately
Encourage the client to increase intake of aspirin-containing medications
questions.explanation: An INR of 5.8 is substantially above the usual therapeutic range for atrial fibrillation and increases bleeding risk. The nurse should withhold the scheduled dose and notify the prescriber for further management and INR monitoring. Protamine reverses heparin rather than warfarin, and aspirin further increases bleeding risk.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies – Adverse Effects and Medication Administration; ACCP Guidance on Management of Elevated INR

questions.stem: A client receiving packed red blood cells develops chills, flank pain, fever, and hypotension 15 minutes after the transfusion begins. Which of the following actions should the nurse take first?
options: Decrease the transfusion rate and reassess the client's vital signs
Administer acetaminophen and continue the transfusion slowly
Stop the transfusion immediately and maintain intravenous access with normal saline using new tubing
Flush the remaining blood through the existing tubing to clear the intravenous line
questions.explanation: These findings suggest an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction, which may rapidly cause shock, kidney injury, and death. The nurse must immediately stop the transfusion and maintain intravenous access with normal saline through new tubing. The nurse should then notify the provider and blood bank and follow the transfusion reaction protocol.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies – Blood and Blood Products

questions.stem: A client receiving total parenteral nutrition (TPN) through a central venous catheter has the infusion unexpectedly interrupted because the solution bag is empty. A replacement bag is not immediately available. The client has no fluid restriction or contraindication to dextrose-containing fluids. Which action should the nurse anticipate while obtaining the replacement TPN?
options: Infuse 0.9% sodium chloride at the previous TPN infusion rate
Leave the central catheter capped until the replacement TPN arrives
Administer a rapid intravenous bolus of regular insulin
Infuse 10% dextrose in water at the prescribed temporary replacement rate
questions.explanation: Abrupt interruption of TPN can cause hypoglycemia, particularly in clients receiving substantial amounts of dextrose. A temporary infusion of 10% dextrose, according to the prescribed or institutional protocol, helps prevent a sudden reduction in glucose delivery. The nurse should also monitor blood glucose and resume TPN when available.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies – Total Parenteral Nutrition

questions.stem: A client with a serum potassium level of 6.7 mEq/L (6.7 mmol/L) is being assessed by the nurse. Which electrocardiographic finding is most strongly associated with this electrolyte abnormality?
options: Prominent U waves following the T waves
Tall, narrow, peaked T waves in multiple leads
Flattened T waves with ST-segment depression
Prolonged QT interval with a clearly visible U wave
questions.explanation: Hyperkalemia commonly produces tall, peaked T waves and can progress to PR prolongation, QRS widening, and life-threatening arrhythmias. A potassium level of 6.7 mEq/L is severe and warrants immediate cardiac monitoring and urgent treatment. Prominent U waves and flattened T waves are more characteristic of hypokalemia.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Reduction of Risk Potential – Laboratory Values and System-Specific Assessments

questions.stem: A client underwent a femoral arterial cardiac catheterization 1 hour ago. The nurse observes a rapidly expanding hematoma at the femoral access site, and the client's blood pressure has decreased from 128/76 mm Hg to 92/58 mm Hg. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Apply firm manual pressure directly over the access site and activate emergency assistance
Elevate the affected leg above heart level and reassess the site in 15 minutes
Assist the client to ambulate to promote circulation in the affected extremity
Apply a warm compress to the hematoma and document the findings
questions.explanation: An expanding femoral hematoma accompanied by hypotension suggests significant arterial bleeding. Immediate firm pressure at the access site helps control hemorrhage while emergency assistance and further treatment are arranged. Delaying intervention can result in substantial blood loss and hemodynamic instability.
questions.subtopic: Potential for Complications of Diagnostic Tests/Treatments/Procedures
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Reduction of Risk Potential – Potential for Complications of Diagnostic Tests/Treatments/Procedures

questions.stem: A client with type 1 diabetes mellitus presents with diabetic ketoacidosis. Laboratory results show a blood glucose of 485 mg/dL (26.9 mmol/L), arterial pH of 7.18, and serum potassium of 3.0 mEq/L (3.0 mmol/L). The provider prescribes intravenous regular insulin and potassium replacement. Which action should the nurse anticipate as the immediate priority before beginning the insulin infusion?
options: Administer intravenous sodium bicarbonate to normalize the arterial pH
Begin the insulin infusion immediately to reduce circulating glucose
Replace potassium while continuing appropriate intravenous fluid therapy
Restrict intravenous fluids until blood glucose falls below 250 mg/dL
questions.explanation: Insulin moves potassium into cells and can worsen existing hypokalemia, potentially precipitating dangerous cardiac arrhythmias. With a potassium level of 3.0 mEq/L, potassium replacement must begin and insulin should be delayed until potassium is above the recommended safety threshold, generally 3.5 mEq/L under current adult DKA guidance. Fluid resuscitation and close electrolyte monitoring remain essential.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Physiological Adaptation – Fluid and Electrolyte Imbalances; Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes Consensus Report (2024)

questions.stem: A client with a history of asthma is admitted with severe wheezing and shortness of breath. After receiving nebulized bronchodilator treatment, the nurse finds that the client is becoming drowsy, has markedly diminished breath sounds, and has an oxygen saturation of 86% despite supplemental oxygen. Which action should the nurse take first?
options: Encourage the client to use pursed-lip breathing and reassess in 20 minutes
Activate the rapid response team and prepare for emergency airway support
Ask the client to demonstrate correct use of a metered-dose inhaler
Obtain a routine peak expiratory flow measurement before contacting the provider
questions.explanation: Drowsiness, severely diminished breath sounds, and persistent hypoxemia in acute asthma indicate impending respiratory failure. The nurse should urgently activate emergency assistance and prepare for advanced airway and ventilatory support. These findings are more concerning than audible wheezing because they may indicate critically reduced airflow and respiratory muscle fatigue.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Physiological Adaptation – Medical Emergencies; Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) Strategy Report

questions.stem: A client with acute pancreatitis has received intravenous fluid resuscitation and prescribed analgesia. Which findings should the nurse recognize as possible evidence of worsening systemic complications? Select all that apply.
options: Blood pressure of 84/50 mm Hg with a heart rate of 124/min
Urine output averaging 45 mL/hr in an adult weighing 70 kg
Oxygen saturation of 88% on room air with increasing respiratory effort
New confusion accompanied by cool, mottled extremities
Temperature of 38.9 degrees Celsius (102 degrees Fahrenheit) with increasing tachycardia
Decreasing abdominal pain after prescribed analgesic administration
questions.explanation: Acute pancreatitis can cause systemic inflammation, capillary leakage, shock, respiratory failure, and organ dysfunction. Hypotension with tachycardia, hypoxemia, altered mental status with poor peripheral perfusion, and fever with worsening tachycardia require prompt reassessment for serious complications. Urine output of 45 mL/hr in a 70-kg adult exceeds the usual minimum target of 0.5 mL/kg/hr, while pain relief after analgesia is generally an expected therapeutic response.
questions.source: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan: Physiological Adaptation – Alterations in Body Systems; American College of Gastroenterology Guideline on Management of Acute Pancreatitis
